versions.derivation_summary: Modeled water-surface elevation (m NAVD88) per Creek Segment. Discharge per NHDPlusV2 reach (NOAA National Water Model v3.0 retrospective, hourly, WY2021–WY2023; California Natural Flows, monthly, 1950–2024) is scaled to each Creek Segment by the USGS drainage-area ratio method (capped at 1; a segment on a creek with no NHDPlusV2 reach of its own uses Drainage-Area Ratio Transfer from the nearest reach, and gets no discharge beyond 1000 m), then converted to WSE with a divided-channel Manning's equation rating curve (n = 0.04 main channel, 0.07 floodplain) on USGS 3DEP 1 m cross-sections. Junction WSE at a shared vertex is the higher of the two neighbouring segments' values. Values are stored as Held WSE Intervals.

versions.derivation_summary: Modeled water-surface elevation (m NAVD88) and junction water depth per Creek Segment. Discharge per NHDPlusV2 reach (NOAA National Water Model v3.0 retrospective, hourly, WY2021–WY2023; California Natural Flows, monthly, 1950–2024) is scaled to each Creek Segment by the USGS drainage-area ratio method (capped at 1; Drainage-Area Ratio Transfer from the nearest reach, and no discharge beyond 1000 m), then inverted on divided-channel Manning's equation rating curves (n = 0.04 main channel, 0.07 floodplain) at the first, middle, and last USGS 3DEP 1 m cross-section of the segment, each with its own bed and a local bed slope. The middle (anchor) section gives the WSE (wse_m); the end sections give the water depth at each junction, shared with the neighbouring segment as the mean of the two end-section depths. The anchor point and the junction beds are static columns of the Creek Segments layer. Time-varying values are stored as Held WSE Intervals: a new interval starts when the anchor WSE or either junction depth changes.

versions.derivation_summary: Modeled water-surface elevation (m NAVD88) and junction water depth per Creek Segment. Discharge per NHDPlusV2 reach (NOAA National Water Model v3.0 retrospective, hourly; California Natural Flows, monthly) is scaled to each Creek Segment by the USGS drainage-area ratio method (segment Q = reach Q × drainageAreaRatio from the crosswalk (USGS drainage-area ratio method, ratio capped at 1), as m1). Flowline channel profile (Manning depth), version 1: Same drainage-area-ratio discharge as m1 and m2, inverted on a divided-channel Manning rating curve cut across a continuous, continuous channel centerline (the TNC flowline smoothed and moved sideways to the lidar valley bottom) at the middle of each Creek Segment. The bed is a smooth, downstream-monotone profile of the flowline; the water depth at each junction is one number per vertex (smoothed mean of the neighbouring anchor depths), so the surface is continuous. The Time Series store true depths only; the segment’s WSE is the surface at the anchor point. Time-varying values are stored as Held WSE Intervals: a new interval starts when the anchor WSE or either junction depth changes.

versions.derivation_summary: Modeled water-surface elevation (m NAVD88) and junction water depth per Creek Segment. Discharge per NHDPlusV2 reach (NOAA National Water Model v3.0 retrospective, hourly; California Natural Flows, monthly) is scaled to each Creek Segment by the USGS drainage-area ratio method (segment Q = reach Q × drainageAreaRatio from the crosswalk (USGS drainage-area ratio method, ratio capped at 1), as m1). Flowline channel profile (Manning depth), version 2: Same drainage-area-ratio discharge as m1 and m2, inverted on a divided-channel Manning rating curve cut across a continuous, channel centerline (the TNC flowline smoothed and moved sideways to the lidar valley bottom) through the creek’s lowest point at the middle of each Creek Segment. The bed is the raw 1 m lidar at the lowest point of every station (no smoothing), breached through road and railroad fills; the flowing depth at each junction is one number per vertex (smoothed mean of the neighbouring anchor depths), and the water surface (bed + flowing depth averaged over ±5 × the flowing depth) is pool-filled along the run, so pools behind steps stand level and deep water drowns the bumps of the raw bed. The Time Series store true depths only; the segment’s WSE is the pool-filled surface at the anchor point. Time-varying values are stored as Held WSE Intervals: a new interval starts when the anchor WSE or either junction depth changes.
